system_prompt:
You are extracting load-bearing passages from one chapter of a guitar method book.

The user will give you the verbatim text of one chapter. Extract every passage
that does any of the following:

- teaches a technique (how to play, fingering, hand position, picking pattern)
- defines a concept (a chord type, a scale, a position system, a terminology)
- gives a rule (when to do X, what to avoid, what to prefer)
- shows a load-bearing example (an exercise that illustrates a method's
  characteristic move)

Output a JSON object with this shape:

  { "quotes": [
      { "topic": "<short topic label>",
        "verbatim_quote": "<exact substring of the input>",
        "why_load_bearing": "<one sentence on why this passage matters>",
        "page": <int, optional>
      },
      ...
  ] }

CRITICAL RULES:
1. `verbatim_quote` MUST be an EXACT substring of the input text. Do not
   paraphrase. Do not add words. Do not fix typos. Copy character-for-character.
2. If you can't find a substantial passage in the input that fits a topic,
   skip the topic — don't fabricate.
3. Skip prose that is purely biographical, motivational, or transitional.
   Keep prose that teaches.
4. Aim for 3-15 quotes per chapter. A chapter with only one load-bearing
   passage gets one quote; a dense chapter gets many.
5. `topic` is a short label (2-6 words). Use the book's own terminology
   when possible.
6. `why_load_bearing` is one sentence in YOUR voice explaining the
   significance — not a paraphrase of the quote.

Chapter 9: The World of Minor 7th & Major 7th Giant Lines
Pages 53-59 of the book.

5) Superimposed IIm7/V7/I Cadences Over                                                            4668




   Dominant 7th Chords
Although we can apply any leading dominant 7th scale over the V degree of a IIm7, V7, I
cadence, when we superimpose them things are quite different because the V7 degree cannot
have tensions anymore thus becoming part of the IIm7 degree dorian.

In other words, in general the superimposed IIm7, V7, I cadences lose the V degree and stay
only with the IIm7 and the Imaj7. However, remember that we can always use the relative
chords from minor and major chords.


Example:

Let's look at cadence in the key of "C" (Dm7, G7, Cmaj7). Therefore we would have 4 different
"colors" to use as superimposition ideas:

• Dm7, Fmaj7 (relative of Dm7) Cmaj7 and Am7 (relative of Cmaj7).

Usually hybrid ideas tend to sound better. However, we can use Dorian ideas over the IIm7 of a
cadence and use Lydian ideas over its relative chord, which will be the IV degree (in this case,
Fmaj7).

Notice that we have an exception which is when the V degree of the superimposed cadence is
the Tritone Substitution from a real dominant chord in the harmony. Then we can choose
                              68


between 2 scales: Lydian Dominant or Dominant Diminished.
                     46




Let's get D7 leading to Gm7 as an example:

In this case we could have the superimposed cadence Ebm7, Ab7, Dbmaj7 used over D7. But
remember that we can always use the 3 chords from this cadence with their relative chords
individually. Apart from that, Ab7 is a Tritone Substitution from D7, which allows us to play
Lydian Dominant or Dominant Diminished ideas over it.


Therefore, in this example we can have 5 different “colors” to use superimposing D7:

1) Ebm7 (Dorian or hybrid)
2) Gbmaj7 - relative of Ebm7 - ( Lydian or hybrid)
3) Dbmaj7 (hybrid)
4) Bbm7 - relative of Dbmaj7 - (hybrid)
5) Ab7 (Lydian Dominant or Dominant Diminished)
